name: Hercules A (Hubble)
blurb: Hercules A, a radio galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: hera-hubble
story: In Hubble's view the elliptical galaxy at the center of Hercules A looks quite ordinary, yet its supermassive black hole drives radio jets, invisible here, that dwarf the visible galaxy. A companion galaxy sits close to its center, and many of the galaxies around it may belong to the same cluster.

claims.text: Hercules A is a radio galaxy
Hercules A is also known as Herc A and 3C 348
In visible light the central elliptical galaxy appears quite ordinary in Hubble's view
The galaxy harbors a supermassive black hole that powers its jets
The radio jets are optically invisible and dwarf the visible galaxy
Hubble's view shows a companion elliptical galaxy very close to the center
Other galaxies in the field may belong to the same galaxy cluster, of which Hercules A is the brightest member
Program 13065 imaged the host galaxy and surrounding cluster of the radio galaxy Hercules A (target HER-A) for a press image
